title: codex-app-mirror release manifest
description: Contract for release-manifest.json, published at https://codexapp.agentsmirror.com/latest/manifest and as a GitHub Release asset on every codex-app-mirror release (stable, beta and linux-preview channels). Fields Codex App Manager parses (see docs/manifest-schema.md) are typed and validated strictly; everything else is intentionally permissive so harmless additions never break publishing or downstream parsing.

schemaVersion.description: Monotonically increasing contract version. Codex App Manager's Windows parser rejects schemaVersion < 2 outright; see docs/manifest-schema.md for the versioning rule.

channel.description: Present on non-stable publications ("beta", "linux-preview"). Absent on the stable channel.

dateTimeLike.description: Either an RFC 1123 HTTP-date (as returned by upstream Last-Modified headers) or an ISO-8601 timestamp. Not constrained to a single `format` keyword because both shapes are real, current output.

packageMoniker.description: Windows MSIX package full name / moniker, e.g. OpenAI.Codex_26.924.2738.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0.

windowsSource.description: Consumed by crates/codex-win-engine/src/manifest.rs::parse_manifest_for_arch in Codex-App-Manager. Every field here is Option in Rust, with a per-architecture entry preferred over this top-level fallback. select_architecture() defaults the requested architecture to "x64" when the caller (the Manager's own update check) doesn't ask for a specific one, and only looks up that single key in `architectures` -- it never falls back to a different architecture's entry (e.g. arm64-only) when the requested one is missing. So the anyOf below requires either a fully-populated top-level fallback (`packageMoniker` + `version`), or `architectures.x64` specifically (validated against windowsArchitectureSource); an architectures map containing only e.g. `arm64` does not satisfy it, matching the parse failure ('missing Windows version') a Manager on the default x64 path would hit.

x64.description: select_architecture() treats an x64 entry with downloadable explicitly false as a hard error (it does not fall back to a different architecture or to Ok(None)), so unlike a generic windowsArchitectureSource entry, this branch only accepts an x64 entry that isn't explicitly marked non-downloadable; a downloadable:false x64 entry only validates via the top-level packageMoniker+version fallback branch above.

windowsArchitectureSource.description: One entry of sources.windows.architectures.<x64|arm64>. When `downloadable` is explicitly false (catalog-only / drifted / unreadable states), version and packageMoniker may be withheld or stale, so the strict requirement below only applies when the architecture is (or may be) downloadable.

macosSource.description: Not read by Codex App Manager today (it installs macOS updates from GitHub Release SHA256SUMS assets instead); kept permissive and only lightly typed for forward-compatibility with docs/manifest-contract.md's documented shape.

sha256.description: Expected to be a lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 digest (or empty) in production; not enforced by pattern here because this field is not Manager-consumed and fixture manifests legitimately use placeholder values.

linuxChannelManifest.description: linux-preview channel (schemaVersion 6 today). Not consumed by Codex App Manager (Linux is not a supported install target), so this branch stays deliberately loose: only the presence and object-ness of sources.linux is enforced.
